data.title: No-confidence motion ‘to be filed this month’
data.description: Opposition parties will submit a no-confidence motion against the government within this month, with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Digital Economy Minister Chaichanok Chidchob the main targets, People’s Party list-MP Parit Wacharasindhu confirmed on Saturday.

data.title: Nene Royal rocking Phuket before AGT final
data.description: Local busker-turned-rock star Nene Royal is inviting fans to attend her live show on Saturday night at Naka Night Market, where she began her music journey in her home province of Phuket — her final show before she flies to the United States to compete in the America’s Got Talent final.

data.title: Zelensky willing to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
data.description: BERLIN - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would be willing to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a G20 summit in December, in an interview released on Saturday, as efforts intensify to end the conflict.

data.title: French police suspect train derailment was sabotage
data.description: CLEON, France - Investigators suspect that a train derailment in northwest France which injured 44, one gravely, was the result of sabotage, a police source told AFP on Saturday.

data.title: Phuket Jewish New Year event cancelled on security grounds
data.description: A Jewish New Year celebration in Phuket was cancelled at the last minute on Friday evening because of concerns raised by Israeli security officials, organisers said.

data.title: ONE Championship: Yod-IQ says Jonathan Haggerty needs Muay Thai win before title shot
data.description: Thailand’s Yod-IQ Or Pimolsri says British rival Jonathan Haggerty should earn a win in Muay Thai before challenging for his newly claimed ONE Championship bantamweight belt – and is serious about going after the Englishman’s kickboxing crown instead.

data.title: Bangkok Blue Line train disrupted, passengers diverted
data.description: Passengers using the MRT Blue Line in Bangkok on Saturday afternoon were forced to alter their routes after a signalling system failure suspended services on a 12-station stretch for more than two hours before repairs were completed.

data.title: Trump lands in Ireland for golf and diplomacy
data.description: DUBLIN - Donald Trump landed in Ireland under tight security Saturday for two days of diplomacy and golf, on a trip that again blurs the lines between his presidency and personal business interests.

data.title: Anxiety grows in Europe over ‘pervert’ AI glasses
data.description: Calls are growing louder in Europe for action against “pervert” smart glasses after secretly filmed video of girls and women appeared online — with a petition in Britain demanding a ban on their sale.

data.title: Bangchak says no leaks found in Bangkok fuel pipeline
data.description: Bangchak Group said no leaks were found in a fuel pipeline along Chuea Phloeng Road in Klong Toey district of Bangkok following an inspection after thousands of litres of oil-contaminated wastewater were reported in the area.

data.title: Xi Jinping lands in India for Brics summit
data.description: NEW DELHI - Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for a Brics summit alongside leaders from India, Russia and Iran as wars, trade and energy test the divided grouping.

data.title: Pathum Thani bank robbery suspect arrested in Bangkok
data.description: PATHUM THANI - Police have arrested a man accused of robbing a bank at gunpoint in Khlong Luang district and later setting fire to the car used in the heist to destroy evidence.

data.title: Phuket property market hits 705bn baht as foreign buyers drive resort demand
data.description: Phuket has more than 90,000 residential units worth 705 billion baht on the market, with resort properties accounting for 52% of supply and foreign demand driving growth.

data.title: Lisa premieres first solo documentary ‘Always Lalisa’ at TIFF on September 11
data.description: Lisa’s Always Lalisa opens in Thai cinemas on October 12, following a year of her life, from Coachella performances to The White Lotus

data.title: Illegal weight-loss products worth B50 million seized
data.description: Unregistered weight-loss injection pens and related materials worth more than 50 million baht were seized on Friday at a house in Nonthaburi, where the seller had been earning an estimated 8 million baht a month from online sales for the past year.

data.title: Senate collusion witness says testimony was forced
data.description: A witness in the Senate collusion case sought to retract his testimony, claiming he had been coerced into implicating the Bhumjaithai Party, according to a leaked document obtained by reporters on Friday.

data.title: Philippine ferry fire death toll reaches 35
data.description: CORON, Philippines - The bodies of passengers killed in a ferry fire off the Philippines arrived at a port near the resort town of Coron, Palawan on Saturday morning, as the country’s coast guard warned the death toll of 35 would grow.

data.title: At least 26 killed in DR Congo school fire stampede
data.description: KINSHASA - A fire and stampede at a school in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo killed at least 26 children, the UN children's agency said on Friday, with some pupils leaping from windows on high floors to escape the carnage.

data.title: Thai-China forum promotes sustainable investment in Rayong
data.description: Thai and Chinese business groups are expanding support for Chinese investors in Rayong, with a forum focusing on rules, jobs, technology and community ties.

data.title: DR Congo school fire stampede death toll rises to 26: UNICEF
data.description: KINSHASA - A fire and stampede at a school in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo killed at least 26 children, the UN children's agency said on Friday, with some pupils leaping from windows on high floors to escape the carnage.

data.title: JIC boss says temple wasn't targeted
data.description: The director of the Thailand-Cambodia Joint Information Centre (JIC) has rejected Cambodia's allegation that Thailand attacked Preah Vihear Temple.

data.title: Neglected facilities draw public scrutiny
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA: Residents of this northeastern province are questioning the management of state-funded projects after a public library and observatory costing nearly 90 million baht were closed and left to deteriorate for more than a decade.

data.title: Witness says testimony was forced
data.description: A witness in the Senate collusion case sought to retract his testimony, claiming he had been coerced into implicating the Bhumjaithai Party, according to a leaked document obtained by reporters yesterday.

data.title: Guru's daily horoscope for Sept 12
data.description: The day of the week you were born on can reveal a lot... Read on.

data.title: Bringing sound to life
data.description: Sounds Of Wireless, the performance series presented by the Royal Bangkok Symphony Music School, returned with another programme that demonstrated just how naturally classical music can speak to audiences when imagination, musicianship and thoughtful presentation come together.

data.title: Suan Dusit Arun's charity Line stickers  support respiratory disease care at  King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital
data.description: In celebration of the first anniversary of Suan Dusit Arun at Dusit Central Park, a new Line sticker set titled "Park For Life: Growing Together" was recently launched.

data.title: Tackling fraud
data.description: Ton instructs his grandma not to answer unknown phone calls. However, the complacent, tech-savvy teenager ends up falling prey to a scam himself. When he downloads a fake computer program, scammers blackmail him by threatening to share his nude photos.

data.title: Jewish cemetery faces probe
data.description: The Interior Ministry has ordered an investigation into the company that owns a Jewish cemetery in Chachoengsao over potential links to nominee businesses and money laundering.

data.title: Capitalising on 'waterway belt'
data.description: Every month, hundreds of containers carrying tissue paper leave southern China for Thailand, making their way by sea to Laem Chabang before the products eventually reach convenience stores, restaurants and households across the country.

data.title: Senators turn on Nakharin
data.description: Pisit Apiwattanapong and some fellow senators have criticised former Constitutional Court president Nakharin Mektrairat for questioning the Senate's political legitimacy and attributing an allegedly false statement to chief charter drafter Meechai Ruchuphan.

data.title: A little family affair
data.description: The upcoming no-confidence debate could produce one of the more intriguing political spectacles in recent parliamentary politics: an uncle and his nephew standing, in effect, on the same side of the chamber against the government.

data.title: House vows OECD-ready parliament
data.description: House Speaker Sophon Zarum has pledged to make parliament a model of good governance as lawmakers and anti-graft campaigners join efforts to help Thailand secure membership of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) by 2028.

data.title: One manager gone and more to follow
data.description: Every manager or head coach in the English Football League knows that at some time they will either get the sack or have to hastily resign before they get the sack. The latter is often termed "leaving by mutual consent" although there is nothing remotely "mutual" about it.
